scope: Operational semantics (declared signal sets) and alert wording. Not a detection result; says nothing about R2's open question.

test_environment.backend: Python 3.12 venv; Redis 7 (docker image redis:7-alpine) on localhost:6379; SQLite; no skipped tests

r3_r4_acceptance_tests.frontend_test: does not call a network-only device degraded for signals it never declared (R3)

test_instability.observed: With an in-process fake Redis server, a different timing-sensitive API test failed on each of two full runs (test_severity_bands..., then test_websocket...). Each passed when run alone.
test_instability.diagnosis: The fake server is about four times slower (API file 157 s vs 40 s) and the processor-thread tests have timing waits; no code defect was found. Not proven by a code change: shown by the real-Redis results above (full suite plus 3 repeats, zero failures).
test_instability.decision: API tests must be run against real Redis (docker run -d --rm --name aegisflow-test-redis -p 6379:6379 redis:7-alpine). Without Redis they skip, which hides the API path; the fake server is not a supported test target.

invariants_tested: No declaration equals declaring all four signals (R3-f)
A declared and an undeclared network-only device give identical scores, severities, patterns, alertability and alert events (R3-d)
A value sent for an unsupported signal is ignored and counted (R3-e)
The alert text names exactly the signals in the alert record, is neutral, and never lists a missing signal as a factor (R4-a to R4-d)
remaining_limitations: Detector effectiveness is unresolved (R2: false-alarm budget inconclusive, detection unmeasured on test data). R3/R4 do not change any score or threshold.
The network-only operating threshold was validated on the simulator only and is poorly calibrated on real traffic (R1, R2).
A declaration is set by an operator and can be wrong; a signal never declared is never watched, so a compromised device cannot be seen losing it.
The wording was not tested with operators; the tests check agreement with the record, not comprehension.
The docker images were not rebuilt or smoke-tested for this release; only the Python and frontend test suites were run.
Persistence of the declaration is tested at the store and API level, not through a full container restart.
